description.narrative:
Insatsen handlar om att ge kärnstöd till Sarajevo Open Center (SOC) strategiska plan 2021-2023. Sida har gett kärnstöd till SOC sedan 2014 och detta är den tredje omgången av stöd till deras strategiska arbete.
SOC är en oberoende feministisk civilsamhällsorganisation som bedriver påverkansarbete för lesbiska, homosexuella, bisexuella, trans och intersex (LGBTI) och kvinnors rättigheter i Bosnien och Hercegovina. SOC arbetar med påverkansarbete gentemot beslutsfattare, utbildning av yrkesverksamma och arbetar med övervakning av genomförande samt forskning inom mänskliga rättigheter inom kvinnors rättigheter och hbtqi-rättigheter. Organisationen ger också skydd och psykologiskt stöd till offer för diskriminering och våld. Organisationen är baserad i Sarajevo och arbetar även i andra delar av Bosnien och Hercegovina (BiH). Tidigare erfarenheter visar att SOC är en stark och professionell organisation som arbetar strategiskt med påverkansarbete gentemot beslutsfattare, samordning inom det civila samhället och forskning. SOC är en viktig aktör för mänskliga rättigheterna och det civila samhället i Bosnien och Hercegovina och uppfattas som en ledare bland CSOer. De är en erkänd aktör som även förespråkar värderingar i linje med EU-närmandet.
Genom insatsen bidrar Sida till följande strategiska mål för SOC: 1) Robust rättslig och politisk ram för mänskliga rättigheter i hela Bosnien och Hercegovina. 2) Stärkta förändringsaktörer i hela BiH. 3) Stärkta värderingar kring mänskliga rättigheter, jämställdhet och inkludering i BiH och i den allmänna debatten.

The contribution is about providing core support to Sarajevo Open Centre (SOC) strategic plan 2021-2023. Sida has provided core support to SOC since 2014 and this is the third round of support to their strategic work.
SOC is an independent feminist civil society organisation and advocacy group which campaigns for lesbian, gay, bisexual, trans and intersex (LGBTI) people and women rights in Bosnia and Herzegovina. SOC works on advocacy towards policy-makers, education of professionals, and works with monitoring of implementation as well as research within the human rights field related to women's rights and lgbtqi-rights. The organization also gives asylum and psychological support to victims of discrimination and violence. The organization is based in Sarajevo and works also in other parts of Bosnia and Herzegovina (BiH). Previous experiences show that SOC is a strong and professional organization who works strategically with advocacy towards decision-makers, coordination within the civil society, and research. SOC is an important player among the human rights and civil society community in Bosnia and Hercegovina, perceived as a leader among COS's. It is a recognized actor that carries EU values.
Through the contribution, Sida contributes to the following strategic goals of SOC: 1) Robust legal and policy human rights based framework throughout BiH. 2) Strengthened agents for change throughout BiH. 3) Strengthening human rights values, equality and inclusion in BH society and public discourse.

The example of results, is based on the last narrative report within this contribution covering 2023. No narrative report for the full agreement period has been requested and established as an agreement condition.
During 2023 SOC has delivered results within all three of the pillars in the results assessment framework, and within all of the 12 thematic areas within the pillars. Below is a presentation of a few examples from each of the three pillars: Pillar I Established legal framework and policy framework for human rights across BiH: * 16 members of the parliament of the Federation of BiH support the adoption of a special law regulating issues of samesex unions: After five years of constant advocacy work by SOC, this group of parliamentarians from different political parties is willing to support legislative inititatives and engage in informed discussion, which can contribute to changing and counteracting homophobic attitudes and open up for positive legislative changes. * A research study on abortion, giving an overview of the existing legal regulation and medical practices was published: this area of work is relatively new to SOC, and the objective is to establish informed cooperation with leading health institutions, raise awareness to the problems of limited access to abortion healthcare services and also to contribute to improving the understanding of abortion as a human right and as a basic healthcare. This work will continue in 2024. * Promotion of paternity leave proposed as one of the measures in the Gender Action Plan for the Sarajevo Canton for the period 2024 2028: SOC has been appointed member of a working group on the new Gender Action Plan for the Sarajevo Canton based on SOC's research in this area, promoting paternity leave to facilitate mothers' access to the labor market. Minster of Labor of FBiH have confirmed that SOC's proposed amendments to the Labor Law, will be taken into account when the Labor Law will be subject to amendments during 2024. Pillar II Empowered agents of change across BiH * 810 LGBTI individuals participated in various events organized by SOC, an informal trans group of 10 individuals was established and began its actitivities, 65 LGBTI individuals received legal advice, 13 strategic litigations were carried out, almost 150 LGBTI individuals received support through peer and/or psychosocial counseling: These are a few of the statistics in relation to support to individuals within the LGBTI community. Through public events SOC creates the possibilities for LGBTI individuals to meet, connect and to be empowered in advocacy and human rights protection. 50% of the legal counceling inquiries were due to hate crime and hate speech. * Strengthening of the Initiative for Monitoring European Integration of BiH and the informal UPR coalition, by building capacities of 23 members: in 2023 SOC continued to empowering civil society to more effectively monitor, report and advocate for the imporvement of human rights, rule of law and democracy. The work within the Initiative and the UPR coalition, grew stronger thanks to 5 training sessions and planned activities. * 173 health workers underwent SOCtraining, 7 public officials attended training on trans rights, 22 politicians were educated on key issues relevatn to gender equality and LGBTI rights, 12 lawyers completed training program on samesex partherships and 346 police cadets at the Police Academy were educated on hate crimes and hate speech: all training activities have led to more engaged and more knowledgeable professionals within key areas, contributing to building an inclusive approach to human rights in BiH. Pillar III Strengthening the values of human rights, equality and inclusion in Bosnian society and public discourse * Work on and publication of 5 key publications presenting detailed resarch analyses in SOC's areas of work: research on attitudes towards homosexual, bisexual, transgender and intersex persons in BiH research on regulation/ availability/practice on abortion in BiH research on the problems and needs of LGBTI individuals in BiH in 2023 Pink Report 2023 Annual report on the human rights situation of LGBTI individuals in BiH others. * In collaboration with the Union of Independent Trade Unions of BiH, SOC made a joint presentation of the publication "Fater on Paternitly Leave Research on Legislative and Administrative barriers to the Use of Paternity Leave by Fathers in BiH.
The example above of results from SOC's work in 2023, is not exhaustive, but illustrates the broad area of work, collaboration with different actors and networks, the longlasting and hard advocacy work and the support to local organisations/centers.
SOC is continuing to work with these areas of work within the new strategic framework for 20242028. See new contribution support to SOC for 20242027, contribution 16806.
